**Build it yourself.** [Read the tutorial](../read/extra-02.qmd) is the other way to read this part.

If you start at this part, make your clone as **Get the project** says, and then run this command. It puts in your clone the files that this part starts from. A file that the project deleted before this part stays, so delete it if `git check` lists it:

```bash
git rm -rq --cached --ignore-unmatch -- :/ && git restore --source ec6a8aa7f9a8 --staged --worktree -- :/
```

```bash

```

The README says in a few lines how to run tally. A user who wants more needs a page of docs. We write it piece by
piece, with a picture. The README then shows how to count from Python, and a recipe checks that the docs are
formatted.

[The code before this part](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/tree/ec6a8aa7f9a8b81ef07c6c8ec69f01307482dc32). [The code after it](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/tree/d6f47209c66d7bb88e4e389e2eb9bc495694df55).

## 2.1 A page on how to run tally {#extra-02.1}

A user who opens the folder `docs` wants one page on how to run tally. Its name has spaces in it, `how to run.md`,
as the names of pages often do.

Apply the patch to [`docs/how to run.md`](#extra-02.1-docs-how-to-run.md-3d8176), from the top of the project:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/17ec79e65166fe1f93c13f94b35e909ca1e36a3c.diff | git apply --include='docs/how to run.md'
```

The patch makes the file `docs/how to run.md`, with a heading and two sections, "Set up" and "Count the words of a
file".

```bash
uv run mdformat --check docs
```

It prints nothing, because the page is formatted as mdformat formats it.

Check your files against this move. The command prints nothing when they match, and otherwise shows what differs:

```bash
git check 17ec79e65166
```

If you are stuck, this command puts the files of this move in place of yours. A file that you made yourself stays:

```bash
git restore --source ec6a8aa7f9a8 --staged -- :/ && git restore --source 17ec79e65166 --staged --worktree -- :/
```

<details open><summary>The patch to <code>docs/how to run.md</code></summary>

````diff
@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+# How to run tally
+
+tally counts the words of a text file.
+
+## Set up
+
+Run this once, and again after each change of the project:
+
+```sh
+just setup
+```
+
+## Count the words of a file
+
+```sh

+```
+
+It prints each word with its count, one word to a line, in the order of the alphabet.
````

## 2.2 The most common words {#extra-02.2}

The page does not say how to keep only the most common words. A section says it, with the option `--top`.

Apply the patch to [`docs/how to run.md`](#extra-02.2-docs-how-to-run.md-3d8176), from the top of the project:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/4a4de50fdb3f29580f612015d62ca81b6c9afe07.diff | git apply --include='docs/how to run.md'
```

The patch adds the section "Only the most common words" at the end of `docs/how to run.md`.

```bash
uv run tally --top 10 data/corpus.txt
```

It prints the ten lines that the section promises, from `127 line` down to `110 code`.

## 2.6 Count from Python {#extra-02.6}

tally is a library as well as a command. A user who writes Python wants to call `count` and `top`. A new section of
the README shows how, in a fenced block of Python.

Apply the patch to [`README.md`](#extra-02.6-README.md-8ec9a0), from the top of the project:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/4cf104b7cd816370bd0a34efc7ff2d2be39f6abb.diff | git apply --include=README.md
```

The patch adds the section "Count from Python" at the end of `README.md`, with a block that counts a short text.

```bash
uv run python -c "from tally import count, top; print(top(count('the cat and the hat'), 2))"
```

It prints `[('the', 2), ('and', 1)]`, as the README says.

Check your files against this move. The command prints nothing when they match, and otherwise shows what differs:

```bash
git check 4cf104b7cd81
```

If you are stuck, this command puts the files of this move in place of yours. A file that you made yourself stays:

```bash
git restore --source 3f033b6e57ab --staged -- :/ && git restore --source 4cf104b7cd81 --staged --worktree -- :/
```

### What changed {#extra-02.6-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="extra-02.6-README.md-8ec9a0"></a>`README.md`: the section "Count from Python", with its block of code. 13 lines added. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/blob/4cf104b7cd816370bd0a34efc7ff2d2be39f6abb/README.md).
  - look at `print(top(counts, 2))`

<details open><summary>The patch to <code>README.md</code></summary>

````diff
@@ -11,3 +11,16 @@ Make the environment, the corpus and the report first. Then count the words of a
 
 `uv run tally --top 10 data/corpus.txt` prints only the ten most common words. `just test` runs the tests, and
 `just report` writes the ten most common words of the corpus to `build/top.txt`.
+
+## Count from Python
+
+tally is a library too. `count` counts the words of a text, and `top` keeps the most common:
+
+```python
+from tally import count, top
+
+counts = count("the cat and the hat")
+print(top(counts, 2))
+```
+
+It prints `[('the', 2), ('and', 1)]`.
````

</details>

[This change on GitHub](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/4cf104b7cd816370bd0a34efc7ff2d2be39f6abb). [The code after it](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/tree/4cf104b7cd816370bd0a34efc7ff2d2be39f6abb).

## 2.9 Count a file from Python {#extra-02.9}

A short text in the README shows little. The block of Python now counts the corpus, and keeps the three most common
words.

Apply the patch to [`README.md`](#extra-02.9-README.md-8ec9a0), from the top of the project:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/a0cde9c7cdd6520d1e82207d6ea78bfc3dba99eb.diff | git apply --include=README.md
```

In the block of Python of `README.md`, the patch adds `from pathlib import Path`, and counts the text of
`data/corpus.txt`. The sentence under the block gives the new output.

This command takes the block of Python out of the README, and runs it:

```bash
sed -n '/^```python$/,/^```$/p' README.md | sed '1d;$d' | uv run python -
```

It prints `[('line', 127), ('class', 126), ('word', 125)]`, as the README says.

Check your files against this move. The command prints nothing when they match, and otherwise shows what differs:

```bash

@@ -17,12 +17,14 @@ Make the environment, the corpus and the report first. Then count the words of a
 tally is a library too. `count` counts the words of a text, and `top` keeps the most common:
 
 ```python

+
 from tally import count, top
 
-counts = count("the cat and the hat")
-print(top(counts, 2))

## 2.10 A recipe that checks the docs {#extra-02.10}

Nobody remembers to run mdformat on each page. A recipe, `just docs`, checks the README and the folder `docs` in one
command.

Apply the patch to [`justfile`](#extra-02.10-justfile-424f0b), from the top of the project:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/cdde9a53f40f29d93721cc8defb7717ea5fb4d93.diff | git apply --include=justfile
```

The patch adds the recipe `docs` at the end of the `justfile`.

```bash
just docs
```

It fails, with exit code 1. mdformat says that `README.md` is not formatted. The section "Run it" has a block of
code indented by four spaces, and mdformat writes a fenced block.

Check your files against this move. The command prints nothing when they match, and otherwise shows what differs:

```bash
git check cdde9a53f40f
```

If you are stuck, this command puts the files of this move in place of yours. A file that you made yourself stays:

```bash
git restore --source a0cde9c7cdd6 --staged -- :/ && git restore --source cdde9a53f40f --staged --worktree -- :/
```

### What changed {#extra-02.10-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="extra-02.10-justfile-424f0b"></a>`justfile`: the recipe `docs`. 4 lines added. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/blob/cdde9a53f40f29d93721cc8defb7717ea5fb4d93/justfile).
  - look at `uv run mdformat --check README.md docs`

<details open><summary>The patch to <code>justfile</code></summary>

```diff
@@ -20,3 +20,7 @@ test:
 report:
     mkdir -p build
     uv run tally --top 10 data/corpus.txt > build/top.txt
+
+# Check that the README and the docs are formatted as mdformat formats them
+docs:
+    uv run mdformat --check README.md docs
```

</details>

## 2.12 The page says how to check the docs {#extra-02.12}

A writer of the docs needs to know that the recipe exists. A last section of the page names it.

Apply the patch to [`docs/how to run.md`](#extra-02.12-docs-how-to-run.md-3d8176), from the top of the project:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/rahuldave/tally/commit/d6f47209c66d7bb88e4e389e2eb9bc495694df55.diff | git apply --include='docs/how to run.md'
```

The patch adds the section "Check the docs" at the end of `docs/how to run.md`.

```bash
just docs
```

mdformat prints nothing, so the new section is formatted too.

Check your files against this move. The command prints nothing when they match, and otherwise shows what differs:

```bash
git check d6f47209c66d
```

If you are stuck, this command puts the files of this move in place of yours. A file that you made yourself stays:

```bash
git restore --source b8347ac5868c --staged -- :/ && git restore --source d6f47209c66d --staged --worktree -- :/
```
